description:
Loneliness is rising. Housing costs are crushing working people. And homelessness continues to grow. In this TEDx talk, Sam Wegert argues the American Dream needs an update—and the answer might not be new construction, but unused space.

Sam explains CoLiving (co living): renting private rooms within a home while sharing common areas, supported by background checks, clear rules, and accountability. He explores how this model can expand housing workforce, build real community, and offer a sustainable option for homeowners and real estate investors who want a scalable way to help their communities. Samuel Wegert is a real estate investor and educator focused on solving housing and loneliness through a shared housing strategy called CoLiving.  Raised as one of eight kids in a small house, Sam learned early that sharing space creates connection and community. As an adult, he experienced the opposite—loneliness—while pursuing the American Dream of independence.  That changed when he began
title: The Lonely American Dream: From Crisis to CoLiving | Samuel Wegert | TEDxCharlotte

description: In this inspiring TEDx talk, Justin Li shares how his strict badminton coach, once labelled the “Devil Coach”, taught him the true power of communication. From fear and misunderstanding to heartfelt connection, he learns to look beyond first impressions and recognise the coach’s tough love and genuine care. This personal journey reveals that listening and open communication can turn intimidating figures into your greatest supporters, unlocking a life-changing magic in every relationship. Justin is a student studying in Chongqing, China. He is passionate about badminton and has won 20 medals through hard work and discipline. Justin used to fear his strict coach, Mr. Zhang, but after a meaningful conversation with his grandmother, he learned to see discipline as a form of care. Now Justin is interested in how communication changes relationships, and he enjoys sharing stories, reading and learning about future technology. author: TEDx Talks
description: Contemporary culture often encourages people to “embrace failure” as if failure itself guarantees improvement. Yet repetition alone does not necessarily lead to learning. The myth of Sisyphus illustrates infinite effort without development: the same action repeated endlessly without change. Failure becomes valuable only when it produces insight, feedback, and adjustment. This talk offers a more precise interpretation of “infinity”: not endless struggle, but humans’ open-ended potential to deepen understanding. Meaningful progress depends not simply on persistence, but on the willingness to rethink assumptions and adapt strategies. Science Teacher & Comedian This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Infinite Effort, Zero Learning: The Sisyphus Problem | Strahinja Kukin | TEDxCSN Youth

A passionate public speaker and world traveler, Henry is dedicated to transforming every stumble into strength. By embracing radical honesty and the courage to say "I don't know yet," you can break free from the illusion of knowledge and finally open the door to true discovery.

description: En esta charla, Verónica explica que creer en uno mismo no siempre es suficiente. Verónica Aliaga es psicóloga clínica con más de diecisiete años de experiencia, dedicada a hacer de la psicología una herramienta accesible, práctica y basada en evidencia. Su trabajo combina clínica, docencia y divulgación, con el propósito de llevar el bienestar y el autoconocimiento más allá de la consulta y hacia los espacios donde las ideas generan cambio. In this presentation, Maya Perest examines loneliness—one of the most prevalent shared experiences of the modern era—through the lenses of displacement, belonging, and music.

Drawing from her personal narrative, Perest shares how her introverted childhood creativity evolved into music over the years, and how this medium reconnected her both to her roots and to other people. She reflects on how the sense of displacement she experienced during her university years away from home unexpectedly led her back to traditional folk songs and her own cultural memory.

This talk serves as a poignant reminder that loneliness is often not about being alone, but about being misunderstood; it illustrates how music and art can bridge human connections by giving a voice to these invisible emotions. author: TEDx Talks
description:
"Very, Very Black: Living Authentically in a World That Wants You Smaller" A talk by by Aiyisha LaTonya Tazashima Obafemi sharing her lived experience on 
What does it mean to be unapologetically yourself when the world was built to make you disappear?
Raised by Black Nationalists, former political prisoners, and revolutionaries — and mentored by legends including Nina Simone, Miriam Makeba, and Gil Scott-Heron — Aiyisha Obafemi didn't just learn about authenticity. She inherited it as a birthright and a responsibility.
In this powerful and deeply personal talk, Aiyisha takes us from the streets of 1980s Black America, where COINTELPRO was dismantling movements and apartheid was ravaging South Africa, to the halls of the music and entertainment industry, where she built a career alongside cousins Grand Puba Maxwell and Tupac Amaru Shakur. Through original poetry, family history, and hard-won wisdom, she explores how music has always been Black America's most radical act of survival —
title: How Black Is It? Very, Very Black! | Aiyisha T. Obafemi | TEDxCollierHeights

description:
Not everything that shapes a sports legend asks to be seen. In this captivating TEDx talk, veteran sports manager Vinod Naidu takes us behind the stadium lights into the world of "obscura"—the invisible game played away from the cameras where an athlete's true legacy is forged.
 
Drawing from over 25 years of shaping some of India’s most iconic sporting narratives and managing elite athletic talent, Vinod pulls back the curtain on high-stakes sports business. He explores the vital role of foresight, gut instinct, crisis management, and the massive, unseen responsibilities that come with guiding an athlete's career path through choices, quiet contract rooms, and critical moments off the field. 

This session will completely shift your perspective on modern sports entertainment, encouraging a deeper appreciation for the subtle, hidden forces that quietly influence the historic outcomes we celebrate on the field.

#TEDxTalks #SportsBusiness #AthleteManagement #Leadership #DecisionMaking

author: TEDx Talks
description:
The way we see the world shapes how we move through it. In this insightful and reflective TEDx talk, psychologist Sukriti Dua explores how our experiences form a unique set of "mental sunglasses" that filter our reality, silently hardening into the invisible patterns that dictate our choices, relationships, and self-worth.
 
Drawing from her journey as a Dance Movement Therapy Facilitator, Sukriti reveals that our minds and bodies are profoundly connected. She decodes how repressed emotions and anxiety manifest physically—from a child's weekly stomach ache to her own personal pattern of constantly falling sick the exact moment the weekend arrives and her body forces her to rest.
 
Ultimately, she shares how we can actively step back, use psychological tools to identify our confirmation biases, and safely clear the fog from our lenses. True growth isn't a perfect upward line, but as Carl Rogers noted: when we accept ourselves as we are, only then can we truly change.

#TEDxTalks #Menta
title: Lenses That Shape Us: Breaking the Patterns That Limit You  | Sukriti Dua | TEDxCITBengaluru

In this talk, Rafayet Rakib explores how comparison silently steals confidence, productivity, and happiness. Drawing from personal experiences and observations, he explains why social media, peer pressure, and the fear of being replaced by artificial intelligence can leave us feeling stuck despite making real progress.
Through simple yet powerful ideas such as controlling the inputs we consume, competing with evidence instead of assumptions, and taking action before confidence arrives, he presents a practical framework for growth in an increasingly distracting world.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Twenty-two years ago, Dr. Mayank D. Chauhan was a student with a dream and a body that suddenly stopped cooperating. A severe slipped disc and radiating lumbar spine pain pointed him toward unavoidable surgery. What he discovered instead changed his life, reshaping his medical purpose from being "saved from surgery" to actively "saving surgery" for others.   

Dr. Mayank—an expert in Orthopedics, Osteopathy, and Chiropractic Medicine—built his entire practice around a vital medical pivot: understanding the difference between temporary pain relief and treating the actual root cause of a problem. He challenges the necessity of invasive procedures, proving that the human body has a tremendous potential to heal if given the right 
environment.
   
Driven by the power of hope and faith, his talk highlights why we must customize treatment to give patients their lives back. Our cracks do not diminish us; they show us that a path to non-invasive healing is always possible.   

#TEDxTalks #Hea
title: What Breaking Taught Me About Healing  | Dr. Mayank D. Chauhan | TEDxCITBengaluru

Stop waiting for the perfect roadmap to start your journey.  

In this powerful TEDx talk, technology leader Ambika J challenges the idea of "readiness" and introduces Genesis—the undeniable pull of curiosity that shapes who we are before we ever have a grand plan. 

Drawing from over 20 years in tech, Ambika shares her personal journey of following her passion against the odds: from a 9-year-old girl booting up 1980s computer labs, to building her own custom home AI assistant (NAADA), to walking across the stage at IIM Bangalore to collect her management certificate with her 18-day-old baby in her arms. 

Her message is simple: The conditions will never be perfect, and you don't need a map handed to you—because you have been drawing it all along.
